newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Steyr to supply over 100,000 engines a year to GAZ.
newsitem.headline: Steyr to supply over 100,000 engines a year to GAZ.

text.p: Austrian auto company Steyr-Daimler-Puch Fahrzeugtechnik AG (SDP) said on Wednesday it will supply more than 100,000 engine kits a year to Russian automaker AO GAZ at the peak of shipments.

"We will deliver over 100,000 units for our licensing agreement with GAZ," Thomas Steiner, marketing director for SDP's Steyr Motorentechnik GmbH, told Reuters. "That's a ballpark figure, but we're talking about the annual capacity."
Previous news reports said annual output would reach only 50,000 units. Steiner offered no explanation for the increase.
GAZ, whose full name is Gorkovsky Avtomobilny Zavod, said earlier it plans to start assembling the engines in early 1997 at its Nizhny Novgorod plant.

SDP, which is owned by Austrian bank Creditanstalt-Bankverein, will start shipments with kits of partly-built engines that GAZ will complete with an increasing amount of its own components, Steiner said.
"At the end of the agreement, GAZ will manufacture the engine 100 percent on its own," Steiner said, declining to cite the agreement's expected duration and value.

"Eventually, GAZ will work completely independently from us, and it will happen quite fast," he said. "GAZ already has all of the capacity to manufacture and machine the engines in place." In December 1995, SDP agreed to supply GAZ with its direct-injection diesel engines in three sizes -- 2.1 litres with four cylinders, 2.7 litres with five cylinders and 3.2 litres with six cylinders.
GAZ said it will install the engines, which SDP began building in 1990, into its Volga sedans and Gazelle light commercial vehicles under plans to modernise its model range.
